channel.title: Updated · Biology
channel.description: Life sciences: discoveries, medicine and biotech

item.title: A daily KRAS-blocking pill plus chemotherapy stops tumour growth in 90% of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer in an early trial
item.description: In a 61-patient phase 1/2 trial, daraxonrasib plus standard chemotherapy shrank tumours in just over 60% of people newly diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer; 76.6% were alive at one year. (BBC News, The Guardian)

item.title: FDA grants accelerated approval to GSK's Nelkarmi for ALK-positive lung cancer that has outgrown earlier drugs
item.description: The FDA cleared neladalkib, a daily pill, for advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer after earlier ALK inhibitors stop working, based on response rates of 49% and 32% in a 222-patient trial. (pharmaphorum, chemXplore)

item.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity
item.description: In two phase 3 trials with 1,019 adults with obesity and painful knee osteoarthritis, weekly retatrutide injections cut pain scores and body weight significantly more than placebo, with more serious side effects. (Thomas J. Schnitzer David J. Hunter Philip G. Conaghan Arya M. Sharma Sue D. Pedersen Kaiyi Chen So Young Park Nune Makarova Kathryn Giblin and Tammy Forresterthe TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA Investigators* · Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine; University of Sydney; University of Leeds; University of Alberta; University of Calgary; Eli Lilly and Company)

item.title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
item.description: A DNA recorder inserted into a fertilized mouse egg wrote an ordered log of cell divisions into the genome, letting researchers rebuild a mouse embryo's cell family tree from the first division to organ formation. (Qi Yu, Haedong Kim, Sophie Seidel et al. · University of Washington School of Medicine; Howard Hughes Medical Institute; Dartmouth College)

item.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia
item.description: Mapping where each cell type sits in the basal ganglia of humans, macaques and marmosets, researchers found a highly stereotyped layout shared across primates and often with mice, with gene gradients laid over discrete compartments. (Madeleine N. Hewitt, Meghan A. Turner, Nelson Johansen et al. · Allen Institute for Brain Science; Princeton Neuroscience Institute; Leiden University Medical Center; Delft University of Technology; The Rockefeller University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Washington University in St. Louis; RIKEN; Kyoto University; University of Washington)

item.title: FDA approves venglustat, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of type 3 Gaucher disease
item.description: The FDA approved Sanofi's Infilbray (venglustat), a daily pill that reaches the brain, after a 43-patient randomized trial showed better neurological scores than standard enzyme infusions at one year. (FDA)

item.title: An off-the-shelf leukemia vaccine extends survival by nine months in a phase 3 trial, its developers report
item.description: In the 126-patient REGAL trial, people with acute myeloid leukemia in second remission who got the WT1 peptide vaccine galinpepimut-S lived a median 24.0 months, against 14.7 months on other treatments. (Memorial Sloan Kettering, BioPharm International)

item.title: Biogen's tau-lowering drug diranersen shows larger effects at two years in early Alzheimer's, in an open-label extension
item.description: Biogen says the twice-yearly 60 mg dose of diranersen slowed decline on the CDR-SB dementia scale by 38% at two years, up from 26% at 18 months, though the comparison comes from an open-label extension. (Biogen (GlobeNewswire), ReachMD)

item.title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
item.description: Eight Homo erectus teeth from two caves in southern China, dated 324,000 to 184,000 years ago, carry chemical signs of a dense rainforest diet and of long journeys in childhood. (K. E. Westaway, R. Joannes-Boyau, W. Liao et al. · Macquarie University, Southern Cross University, Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Vertebrate Palaeontology and Palaeoanthropology)

item.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
item.description: Mining 85,123 genetic datasets, researchers found egoviruses, the closest known relatives of poxviruses, in the guts of humans and livestock worldwide, hinting that the smallpox family began in animal guts. (Morgan Gaïa, Ulysse Guyet, Hans-Joachim Ruscheweyh et al. · French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS))

item.title: Nicotinamide Riboside for Patients With Early-Stage Parkinson Disease: The NOPARK Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description: In a 410-person Norwegian trial, a year of the NAD-boosting supplement nicotinamide riboside did not help early Parkinson's disease; symptom scores were slightly worse than with placebo. (NOPARK trial investigators (study director: Charalampos Tzoulis) · Haukeland University Hospital, University of Bergen)

item.title: FDA approves adrabetadex, the first drug shown to lengthen survival in infantile-onset Niemann-Pick disease type C
item.description: The FDA approved Lembaz (adrabetadex), a spinal injection given every two weeks, after treated patients with early-onset Niemann-Pick disease type C lived a median 8.5 years versus 4.9 years in matched controls. (FDA)

item.title: AriBio's oral Alzheimer's drug AR1001 slows decline in patients taking no other dementia drug, but not in its full phase 3 trial
item.description: In a 1,535-patient phase 3 trial, the daily pill AR1001 slowed decline by 31% among 604 patients on no other dementia drug, meeting a prespecified goal, but showed no significant effect overall. (MoneyToday, iNews24)

item.title: Nicotinamide Riboside for Patients With Early-Stage Parkinson Disease
item.description: In a 410-person randomized trial, a year of the NAD-boosting supplement nicotinamide riboside did not slow early Parkinson's disease; symptom scores ended slightly worse than with placebo. (Charalampos Tzoulis and the NOPARK investigators · University of Bergen; Haukeland University Hospital)

item.title: FDA approves giredestrant, a Roche pill for advanced breast cancer with ESR1 mutations
item.description: The FDA approved Roche's giredestrant (Wilserdly) with everolimus for advanced ER-positive breast cancer carrying an ESR1 mutation, after a trial showed a longer delay before the cancer worsened. (Genentech (press release via Yahoo Finance), Medical Daily, STAT)

item.title: A bladder-instilled immunotherapy cut cancer recurrence by 68% in a phase 3 trial, CG Oncology reports
item.description: In a 367-patient randomized trial, CG Oncology's cretostimogene lowered the risk of bladder cancer returning after surgery by 68% compared with monitoring alone, according to topline company results. (Quiver Quantitative (summary of CG Oncology press release), PharmaShots, STAT)

item.title: CDC scientists count 112 measles infections in pregnancy and 13 babies born with measles since 2025
item.description: A preliminary CDC analysis in NEJM Evidence documents 112 confirmed measles cases in pregnant women and 13 newborns with congenital measles in the United States since the start of 2025. (The New York Times, NBC News (Associated Press), Associated Press via KSLA)

item.title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age
item.description: In a two-year randomized trial of 167 children aged 6 to 11 with obesity, weekly semaglutide lowered BMI by 13.5% at 68 weeks while it rose 2.7% on placebo; stomach side effects were common. (Ania M. Jastreboff Nina M. Harder-Lauridsen Michelle Van Name Antje Körner Aaron S. Kelly Daniel Weghuber Jens-Christian Holm Christine Frithioff-Bøjsøe Shilpa Middolu Tina Buch and Martin Wabitschthe STEP Young Investigators* · Yale University School of Medicine; Ulm University Medical Center; University of Leipzig)

item.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
item.description: Tested in 844,108 adults in four countries, a definition of obesity that adds waist measures and organ function to BMI separated people at high risk of death from those at modest risk. (An Pan, Shengping Yang, Rafael Ramos et al. · King's College London; Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Kailuan General Hospital; North China University of Science and Technology; Pennington Biomedical Research Center; University of Colorado Anschutz; University of Girona; Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore)

item.title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
item.description: Stone points from a 125,000-year-old lakeshore in Saudi Arabia's Empty Quarter carry residues suggesting they were mounted on shafts and possibly tipped with plant poison. (Chris Clarkson, Gilbert J. Price, Amir Kalifi et al. · Griffith University; King Abdullah University of Science and Technology; Saudi Heritage Commission)

item.title: FDA declines to approve ivonescimab for lung cancer because the trial did not show a significant survival gain
item.description: The FDA rejected Summit's ivonescimab plus chemotherapy for previously treated EGFR-mutated lung cancer, saying slower tumor progression without a statistically significant survival benefit was not enough. (The New York Times, Reuters (via SRN News), OncoDaily)

item.title: The US has lost its measles elimination status after 26 years, people close to the Pan American Health Organization's review say
item.description: An expert commission reporting to the Pan American Health Organization has concluded that measles is again spreading continuously in the US, ending a status held since 2000, according to people familiar with the review. (CNN, KFF Health News (via NPR))

item.title: Six months in, Congo's Ebola outbreak still adds up to 500 cases a week as attacks on health workers disrupt the response
item.description: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak centered on the Democratic Republic of the Congo has passed 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths, and WHO and UN officials say armed violence is now blocking containment. (CIDRAP, ECDC, CDC)

item.title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement
item.description: In a trial of 18,883 joint replacement patients, aspirin was not shown to prevent clots and deaths as well as rivaroxaban or warfarin, which in turn were not shown to be as safe. (Vincent D. Pellegrini Carol A. Lambourne Laurence S. Magder Patricia D. Franklin Jay S. Magaziner Brook I. Martin Richard Iorio Kevin L. Garvin Michael A. Mont Wayne E. Moschetti Antonia F. item.title: Single-cell, multi-region profiling of the macaque brain across the lifespan
item.description: An atlas of 5.3 million cells from 11 brain regions of 55 rhesus macaques charts how each cell type changes with age and finds overlap with the molecular signatures of Alzheimer's disease. (Wei Yang, Kelsi L. Watkins, Alex R. DeCasien et al. · University of Washington; Arizona State University; National Institute on Aging; University of Pennsylvania; University of Alabama at Birmingham; Caribbean Primate Research Center, University of Puerto Rico)

item.title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
item.description: Fruit flies evolving in outdoor and indoor cages changed pigmentation in a direction a genetic map could predict, but which genes did the changing was largely unpredictable. (J. A. Smiley-Rhodes, M. C. Bitter, S. Berardi et al. · Stanford University; University of Pennsylvania; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub)

item.title: FDA approves durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin around surgery for bladder cancer patients who cannot take cisplatin
item.description: The FDA approved an immunotherapy plus antibody-drug conjugate given before and after bladder removal for patients who cannot or will not take cisplatin, after a 695-patient trial showed longer event-free and overall survival. (FDA, The ASCO Post)

item.title: US measles deaths climb as the CDC's tally reaches six and states report ten, with cases above 5,400
item.description: The CDC now counts six US measles deaths in 2026 while state health departments report ten, cases have reached 5,412, and a regional health body is weighing whether the US has lost measles-elimination status. (CIDRAP, PolitiFact)

item.title: China approves Lilly's orforglipron, the first GLP-1 weight-loss pill cleared there
item.description: China's drug regulator approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron tablets for adults with obesity, or overweight plus a related condition, making it the first oral GLP-1 drug for weight management in the country. (Pharmaceutical Technology, Plataforma Media)

item.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
item.description: In a non-randomized Dutch study of 231 young adults in refractory cardiac arrest, helicopter teams starting ECMO on scene saw 40% survive to discharge versus 20% with conventional care. item.title: An LHX2-DACH1 regulatory innovation drives basal progenitor expansion in the primate neocortex
item.description: A small DNA switch that controls the gene DACH1, with a feature shared among primates, helps the developing cortex make more of a special stem cell abundant in primate brains, in organoids and mice. (Pei-Shan Hou, Ching-Yu Chuang, Feng-Lan Chiu et al. · National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University; Academia Sinica; Kyoto University)

item.title: A multi-tissue atlas of genetic regulatory effects in sheep
item.description: SheepGTEx maps how DNA variants control gene activity across 51 sheep tissues and cell types, and ancient DNA shows breeding favored variants acting in just one or a few tissues, such as skin. (Mian Gong, Ziyang Zhuang, Xiangrong Sun et al. · Aarhus University)

item.title: The American Cancer Society now recommends regular PSA screening for prostate cancer, every two years from age 50
item.description: The American Cancer Society's new guideline recommends a PSA blood test every two years for average-risk men aged 50 to 69, and yearly from 45 for Black men and men with strong family history. (American Cancer Society, The New York Times)

item.title: FDA approves pimicotinib, a once-daily pill, for joint tumors that are hard to remove surgically
item.description: The FDA approved EMD Serono's pimicotinib for symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor after a placebo-controlled trial in which 56% of treated patients responded, against 3.2% on placebo. (FDA, HMP Global Oncology)

item.title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma
item.description: In a phase 3 trial of 1,137 people with resected high-risk melanoma, adding a personalized mRNA therapy to pembrolizumab raised two-year recurrence-free survival from 70.0% to 82.2%. (Georgina V. Long Muhammad A. Khattak Helen J. Gogas Dirk Schadendorf Ana Arance Matteo S. Carlino Piotr Rutkowski Gareth Rivalland Antoni Ribas Janice M. Mehnert Patrick A. item.title: Cross-species multiomic atlas of the primate basal ganglia
item.description: A cell-by-cell atlas of 1.8 million nuclei from human, macaque and marmoset basal ganglia finds 61 cell types conserved over 76 million years and maps psychiatric and neurodegenerative risk onto specific cells. (Nelson J. Johansen, Yuanyuan Fu, Matthew Schmitz et al. · Allen Institute)

item.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
item.description: In mice, the gut antibody IgA slows the renewal of the colon lining through a surface protein called DMBT1, and its absence raises susceptibility to colorectal tumors. (Gregory P. Donaldson, Gabriella Lima dos Reis, Marwa Saad et al. · The Rockefeller University)

item.title: Beam's base-edited sickle cell therapy keeps patients free of severe pain crises for a year in its pivotal trial
item.description: Beam Therapeutics says its one-time base-edited cell therapy, risto-cel, met its main goal of 12 months without severe pain crises in a 49-patient single-arm trial, and plans a US filing. (PharmaShots (summary of Beam's press release), BioPharm International)

item.title: A Lancet Psychiatry analysis compares how well 21 antidepressants keep depression at bay over months to years
item.description: Pooling 115 studies longer than 12 weeks, researchers found escitalopram, duloxetine and agomelatine somewhat more likely than fluoxetine to bring lasting improvement; experts call the differences modest. (The New York Times, BBC News)

item.title: Everyone in a 100,000-person All of Us sample carries gene variants that affect medicines, and a quarter got an affected drug
item.description: A Pitt-led analysis of nearly 100,000 genomes found every participant carried at least one drug-relevant variant (median nine), 24.4% had been prescribed an affected drug, and over 17,000 variants were new. (University of Pittsburgh via Medical Xpress, STAT, Science Translational Medicine)
